Tailwind v4 `@theme inline` may not be generating the `text-bone` utility class correctly despite the custom token definition. The hero text might also remain invisible because the motion animation failed to run or was suppressed by reduced-motion preferences.

The Canvas layer uses `-z-10` to sit behind the hero content, yet its parent container may still create a stacking context that obscures the section. The grain overlay at `z-60` and the navigation at `z-50` could also be interfering with the layering.

The missing `text-bone` class should fall back to the default body color, so the text ought to be visible. The real culprit may be the motion blur filter paired with zero opacity; if the animation never completes, the heading stays invisible. The duplicate Resume button is caused by the viewport sitting between the `md:` breakpoint thresholds, where both the desktop nav link and the mobile resume button are rendered simultaneously.

The duplicate Resume links are both present in the DOM, which should be impossible under normal Tailwind breakpoint logic. Since the build succeeded and other utilities function correctly, the issue likely stems from a specificity override or a Tailwind compilation quirk that suppresses the responsive visibility classes.

The hero content may simply be positioned below the visible viewport. The duplicate Resume button is a confirmed Tailwind breakpoint failure, since the desktop navigation renders while the mobile resume link also appears. The next step is to inspect computed styles via CDP to confirm why the responsive visibility classes are not taking effect.

The hero section uses `justify-end` inside a `min-h-100dvh` container, so its content should sit at the bottom of the viewport. If the screenshot instead shows the top of the page, the content may have zero height or be fully transparent. I will capture another screenshot after scrolling, or use CDP to inspect exact element positions and colors.
